questions.statement: What does the causative sentence I had my car repaired mean?
questions.context: A student is explaining what happened to her car last week.

options.text: Another person repaired my car for me.
options.feedback: This is right: had plus object plus past participle means that someone else did the repair on my behalf.

options.text: I repaired my car with my own hands.
options.feedback: This would be the active sentence I repaired my car, where I am the one doing the work, not the causative.

options.text: My car has never needed any repair.
options.feedback: The sentence describes a completed repair, so it says nothing about the car never needing one.

options.text: I was repairing my car at that moment.
options.feedback: The progressive was repairing describes my own action in progress, not work arranged for me.

questions.explanation:
In have plus object plus past participle the subject arranges the action but does not perform it, so I had my car repaired means a garage did the work.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the pattern get plus person plus to infinitive correctly?
questions.context: A teacher writes two causative patterns on the board for the class.

options.text: She got her brother carry the boxes.
options.feedback: The bare infinitive carry is used after have plus a person, not after get plus a person.

options.text: She got her brother to carry the boxes.
options.feedback: This is right: after get plus a person the verb needs the to infinitive, so to carry is the correct form.

options.text: She got her brother carried the boxes.
options.feedback: The past participle carried belongs to get plus object plus participle, where the object is a thing rather than a person who acts.

options.text: She got her brother carrying the boxes.
options.feedback: The ing form carrying cannot follow get plus a person in this causative pattern.

questions.explanation:
The pattern get someone to do something always keeps the to before the verb: she got her brother to carry the boxes.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement about have and get in the causative is correct?
questions.context: Two students compare how formal the two causative verbs sound.

options.text: Get can only take a past participle.
options.feedback: Get also takes a person with a to infinitive, as in get someone to help, so the claim is too narrow.

options.text: Have can never take a past participle.
options.feedback: Have takes a past participle in have something done, so this claim is false.

options.text: Have sounds more formal than get in the causative.
options.feedback: This is right: have is the neutral or formal choice, while get is common in informal speech.

options.text: Get is always more formal than have.
options.feedback: Get is the informal option, not the more formal one, so the sentence reverses the register.

questions.explanation:
Both verbs build the causative, but have fits formal writing while get is typical of everyday conversation.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the causative have with a past participle correctly?
questions.context: A student proofreads a paragraph about home repairs.

options.text: We had the windows clean last week.
options.feedback: The bare adjective clean cannot serve as the past participle in this causative pattern.

options.text: We had cleaned the windows last week.
options.feedback: Had cleaned is the past perfect active, which says we cleaned them ourselves, not the causative.

options.text: We had the windows cleaning last week.
options.feedback: The ing form cleaning is not the participle this pattern requires.

options.text: We had the windows cleaned last week.
options.feedback: This is right: the pattern is have plus object plus past participle, so cleaned is the correct form.

questions.explanation:
The causative have takes an object and a past participle, so the windows were cleaned by someone we arranged.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I had my hair ___ at the new salon yesterday. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A girl tells her friend about her appointment at a new salon.

options.text: cut
options.feedback: This is right: cut is the past participle of this irregular verb, and it fits have plus object plus participle.

options.text: cutted
options.feedback: Cutted is not a real form; the verb cut keeps the same form in the past and the participle.

options.text: cutting
options.feedback: Cutting is the ing form and cannot fill the participle slot in have something done.

options.text: to cut
options.feedback: The to infinitive to cut does not follow the object in this causative pattern.

questions.explanation:
After have plus object the verb appears as a past participle, and cut is unchanged because it is irregular.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Maria got her brother ___ her with the move. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A student describes how she moved to a new flat last month.

options.text: help
options.feedback: The bare infinitive help follows have plus person, not get plus person.

options.text: to help
options.feedback: This is right: get plus a person takes the to infinitive, so to help is the correct form.

options.text: helped
options.feedback: The past participle helped would belong to get plus a thing plus participle, not to a person who acts.

options.text: helping
options.feedback: The ing form helping is not allowed after get plus person in this pattern.

questions.explanation:
The pattern get someone to do something keeps the to before the verb: Maria got her brother to help her.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence means that a professional did the work for the family?
questions.context: A family talks about the damage caused by a storm.

options.text: We repaired our roof after the storm.
options.feedback: The active repaired says that we did the work ourselves, which is the opposite meaning.

options.text: We were repairing our roof after the storm.
options.feedback: The progressive were repairing also shows us doing the work, not a professional.

options.text: We had our roof repaired after the storm.
options.feedback: This is right: the causative had plus object plus participle shows that someone else did the repair.

options.text: Our roof repairs after the storm.
options.feedback: This word order is not a grammatical English sentence at all.

questions.explanation:
The causative had our roof repaired places the action in someone else's hands, so a professional did the job.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I did not have my car ___ before the trip. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A driver explains what he did not arrange before a long trip.

options.text: service
options.feedback: The bare verb service cannot follow the object in have something done.

options.text: servicing
options.feedback: The ing form servicing is not the participle this pattern needs.

options.text: to service
options.feedback: The to infinitive to service does not fit after the object here.

options.text: serviced
options.feedback: This is right: the negative causative keeps the past participle serviced after the object.

questions.explanation:
Negation does not change the pattern, so did not have my car serviced keeps object plus past participle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The printer is broken, but I will get it ___ tomorrow. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: An office worker reports a problem with a machine.

options.text: fixed
options.feedback: This is right: get plus object plus past participle uses fixed for a machine that someone will repair.

options.text: fix
options.feedback: The bare verb fix is used with get plus a person, not with a thing such as it.

options.text: fixing
options.feedback: The ing form fixing does not fill the participle slot in get something done.

options.text: to fix
options.feedback: The to infinitive to fix follows get plus a person, not get plus a thing.

questions.explanation:
With a thing as the object, get takes a past participle, so the printer will be fixed by someone.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence places the time expression correctly in a causative sentence?
questions.context: A teacher marks a student's sentence about a garage visit.

options.text: She had yesterday her car repaired.
options.feedback: The adverb yesterday cannot sit between had and its object, so the order is wrong.

options.text: She had her car repaired yesterday.
options.feedback: This is right: the time expression comes after the whole causative phrase at the end of the sentence.

options.text: She had her car yesterday repaired.
options.feedback: The adverb cannot split the object her car from the participle repaired.

options.text: Yesterday she had repaired her car.
options.feedback: Had repaired is the past perfect active, so this is not the causative at all.

questions.explanation:
The causative block have plus object plus participle stays together, and the time expression follows it.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses have plus a person plus the bare infinitive?
questions.context: A homeowner describes how the wiring was checked.

options.text: I had the wiring checked by the electrician.
options.feedback: This is the other causative pattern, have plus object plus past participle, not have plus person.

options.text: I had the electrician to check the wiring.
options.feedback: After have plus a person the verb must be bare, so to check is wrong.

options.text: I had the electrician check the wiring.
options.feedback: This is right: have plus a person takes the bare infinitive check, with no to.

options.text: I had checked the wiring by the electrician.
options.feedback: Had checked is the past perfect active and does not fit the causative meaning.

questions.explanation:
When a person follows have, the verb is a bare infinitive: I had the electrician check the wiring.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence means that I persuaded the mechanic to look at the engine?
questions.context: A driver tells a friend how she persuaded a mechanic to help.

options.text: I got the engine to look at the mechanic.
options.feedback: This reverses the roles, because an engine cannot look at a mechanic.

options.text: I got the engine looked at the mechanic.
options.feedback: The order is jumbled and the participle looked does not fit the person as agent.

options.text: I got looking at the engine the mechanic.
options.feedback: This word order is not grammatical and the ing form is out of place.

options.text: I got the mechanic to look at the engine.
options.feedback: This is right: get plus a person takes the to infinitive, and the person is the one who looks.

questions.explanation:
With get, the person who acts comes right after the verb and takes the to infinitive: got the mechanic to look.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question asks correctly about a service someone arranged in the past?
questions.context: A clinic receptionist asks a patient about a past eye test.

options.text: Did you have your eyes tested last year?
options.feedback: This is right: after did the verb is the base have, followed by object and past participle.

options.text: Did you had your eyes tested last year?
options.feedback: The auxiliary did already marks the past, so the main verb cannot also be had.

options.text: Did you have tested your eyes last year?
options.feedback: Have tested your eyes is the present perfect active, not the causative pattern.

options.text: Do you had your eyes tested last year?
options.feedback: Do does not combine with had, and the tense does not match the past question.

questions.explanation:
In questions the auxiliary did carries the tense, so the causative keeps have plus object plus participle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is the best formal causative choice for a written report?
questions.context: A journalist writes a formal report for a company newsletter.

options.text: The company got the report translated into Spanish.
options.feedback: This is grammatical but get is informal and better suited to speech than to a report.

options.text: The company had the report translated into Spanish.
options.feedback: This is right: have plus object plus past participle is the neutral and formal causative.

options.text: The company got translate the report into Spanish.
options.feedback: Get cannot take the bare verb translate directly after the object.

options.text: The company had translate the report into Spanish.
options.feedback: Have cannot take the bare verb translate directly after the object either.

questions.explanation:
Formal writing prefers have in the causative, so had the report translated suits the newsletter.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which pair of sentences has the same meaning?
questions.context: A student studies two causative sentences with the same meaning.

options.text: I will get the plumber to fix it. = I will fix it myself.
options.feedback: In the first sentence the plumber does the work, not the speaker, so the meanings differ.

options.text: I will have the plumber fix it. = The plumber will have me fix it.
options.feedback: The second sentence reverses who gives the order, so the two meanings are opposite.

options.text: I will get the plumber to fix it. = I will have the plumber fix it.
options.feedback: This is right: get plus person plus to infinitive and have plus person plus bare infinitive describe the same arrangement.

options.text: I will get the plumber to fix it. = The plumber will get me to fix it.
options.feedback: Here the plumber becomes the one who arranges, so the meaning changes completely.

questions.explanation:
The patterns get someone to do and have someone do express the same idea with a different causative verb.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses get plus object plus past participle correctly?
questions.context: A man prepares for a job interview and thinks about his clothes.

options.text: He got cleaned his jacket before the interview.
options.feedback: The participle cleaned cannot come before the object in this pattern.

options.text: He got his jacket clean it before the interview.
options.feedback: The pronoun it has no place here and makes the sentence ungrammatical.

options.text: He got his jacket to clean before the interview.
options.feedback: The to infinitive to clean follows get plus a person, not get plus a thing.

options.text: He got his jacket cleaned before the interview.
options.feedback: This is right: get plus object plus past participle orders the words as got his jacket cleaned.

questions.explanation:
When the object is a thing, get takes a past participle, so he arranged for his jacket to be cleaned.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best paraphrases A mechanic will service my car tomorrow?
questions.context: A student rewrites a sentence about a car service for homework.

options.text: I will have my car serviced tomorrow.
options.feedback: This is right: the causative have plus object plus participle keeps the mechanic as the one who works.

options.text: I will service my car tomorrow.
options.feedback: The active service says that I do the work myself, which changes the meaning.

options.text: My car will service me tomorrow.
options.feedback: This reverses the roles and makes the car the one that acts.

options.text: I will be serviced my car tomorrow.
options.feedback: The passive be serviced cannot be combined with my car as object this way.

questions.explanation:
The paraphrase keeps the same worker and the same action, so the causative have my car serviced is the match.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.context: A student checks four sentences before handing in an essay.

options.text: She had her assistant booked the tickets.
options.feedback: The past participle booked cannot follow a person in the have causative.

options.text: She had her assistant book the tickets.
options.feedback: This is right: have plus a person takes the bare infinitive book, with no to and no past form.

options.text: She had her assistant to book the tickets.
options.feedback: The to infinitive to book is wrong after have plus a person.

options.text: She had booked her assistant the tickets.
options.feedback: This order and meaning are jumbled and do not form the causative.

questions.explanation:
The pattern have someone do something uses the bare infinitive, so had her assistant book is correct.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which causative sentence matches The documents were translated by a specialist?
questions.context: A lawyer explains how a translation was arranged.

options.text: We had translated the documents by a specialist.
options.feedback: Had translated is the past perfect active and does not carry the causative meaning.

options.text: We had the specialist translated the documents.
options.feedback: The pattern needs the specialist to be followed by a bare infinitive, not by the documents.

options.text: We had the documents translated by a specialist.
options.feedback: This is right: have plus object plus past participle keeps the specialist as the doer.

options.text: We were had the documents translated.
options.feedback: The auxiliary were cannot precede had in this way, so the sentence is ungrammatical.

questions.explanation:
The passive can be recast as a causative by naming the arranger as subject: we had the documents translated.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence describes arranging for work that is already completed before now?
questions.context: A traveler talks about a document she arranged some time ago.

options.text: I have my passport renewed.
options.feedback: The present simple have my passport renewed usually describes a habit, not a finished result.

options.text: I had my passport renew.
options.feedback: The bare verb renew cannot follow the object in the causative.

options.text: I have renewed my passport.
options.feedback: Have renewed is the present perfect active, which says I renewed it myself.

options.text: I have had my passport renewed.
options.feedback: This is right: have had plus object plus participle is the present perfect causative, so the work is done.

questions.explanation:
The present perfect causative have had something done shows an arrangement completed before the present moment.
---
